steps.hints: ❓ Did you use the documentation for help with updating the values that determine the Ball sprite’s movement?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the Ninja:

❓  What value might be multiplied with the value of the status bar to increase the Ball sprite’s velocity?


Solution:

Inside the conditional of the A button released event, the force should be assigned to the status bar’s value multiplied by a number, such as 2, to increase the Ball sprite’s velocity.


Ask the Ninja:

❓ What sprite property represents the horizontal opposing force against the motion of a sprite?


Solution:

At the beginning of the project, the Ball sprite should be assigned a larger y-acceleration (ay) value, causing it to fall to the ground with a greater force and increasing its bounce. It should also be assigned an x-friction (fx) value greater than 0, causing the Ball sprite’s movement to slow gradually after it’s hit.


Ask the Ninja:

❓  What function returns the value of a number without its sign (+/-)?


Solution:

The abs function should be added inside the if condition of the onHitWall event so that it checks if the absolute value of the Ball sprite is greater than 50, before reducing its speed. The condition should look like this: 

(Math.abs(sprite.vy) > 50)
steps.instructions:
Fix the bugs in the code to create a working project!


When the user releases the A button, the force at which the Ball sprite is hit should be greater than the status bar’s actual value shown on screen.


After the Ball sprite is hit, it should gradually slow down as it hits wall tiles, not bounce endlessly off of them. The Ball sprite should be pulled down to the ground to create a large bounce.


If the Ball sprite’s bounce is too large, its velocity should be gradually decreased regardless of the direction it is bouncing.


Use the functions in the code menu and the code completion tool to create a working version of this project!

subgroups.title: Debugging Sprite Physics
subgroups.introduction: Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!
